newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. June durables rise 2.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. June durables rise 2.3 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Commerce Department said June orders for durable goods rose 2.3 percent compared to a revised 0.4 percent decrease in May.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected a 1.4-percent rise in orders in June.

DAVID SLOAN, SENIOR ECONOMIST, I.D.E.A. INC: "The 0.8-percent rise in ex-transportation orders is reasonable. (Overall,) it's a ... figure indicating a healthy economy, but there are no surprises here."

Sloan, who was speaking on Reuters Financial Televsion, said he expected third-quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth to be "strong," adding that the pace of expansion in the fourth-quarter would be even more robust.
DAN SETO, SENIOR ECONOMIST, THE NIKKO SECURITIES CO

INTERNATIONAL INC: "Aircraft orders is the story ... we are getting a bit of a bounce back from non-aircraft orders, so it's a bit of a recovery there. I think most people are comfortable with moderate growth and this is a report that is consistent with that."
BRIAN FABBRI, CHIEF NORTH AMERICAN ECONOMIST, PARIBAS

CORP: "Overall, it is a great piece of news. We are generating more growth, but no inflation. (June) durable goods represent growth in manufacturing for the quarter ahead. If there were any surprises it is that computer technology orders were flat on the month after rising strongly in prior months."
CARY LEAHEY, CHIEF U.S. ECONOMIST, HIGH FREQUENCY
ECONOMICS: "The number is overstated by the transportation rebound. But if you take out transportation, it's still a solid number.
"Most people were looking for only a small gain in ex-transportation, but we got an increase of 0.8 percent, so that's 3/4 of a percentage point above expectations," Leahey added.
ASTRID ADOLFSON, FIRST VICE PRESIDENT AND AN ECONOMIST,

MCM MONEYWATCH INC: "It confirms that durables are in an uptrend ...I don't think there's any question about that ... It confirmes that we're in a rebound in the third quarter. July has started off in a slow mode ... but we think they'll come back."

JAMES PADINHA, ECONOMIST, BRIEFING.COM: "The fears of a huge aircraft gain pushing up the total series as much as 5.0, 6.0, 7.0 percent did not come through. (But) I'm glad to see some of the aircraft orders did come through ... and that's more consistent with a lot of the orders volume that Boeing has been reporting.

"Looking at some of the core categories, we had a good gain in ex-transport orders. Non-defense capital goods shipments were up ... and that bolds well for the fixed investment (component) of the GDP.

"The report confirms that the production side of the economy is still strong. That has been the discrepancy. You've had really strong production ... but we just haven't seen demand kick back in yet," he added.
